context: constraint: a malformed config must never fail the host command — degrade to shipped defaults plus one warning
constraint: must not narrow what parses cleanly today; the repo's own .specify/companion.yml is the live regression fixture
intent: Make a companion.yml the constrained reader cannot handle fail loudly with the documented malformed warning, instead of returning a silently truncated config.
expectations: Do not implement YAML anchor/alias support
Do not narrow what the reader accepts today
Do not change any behavior outside the config reader
approach: Teach the constrained YAML reader to recognise the four unsupported shapes (anchor, alias, tab indentation, block scalar) with a per-line guard, and add a general check that the parser read the file to its last line. Every one raises, which the loader's existing failure path turns into the documented malformed warning plus shipped defaults. The checks look only at the first token of a key or an unquoted value, so nothing that parses today is narrowed.

decisions.decision: Detect the unsupported syntax and raise, rather than implement anchor support
decisions.why: The failure table already reports an unreadable file correctly; the reader just never noticed. Detection is a few line-shape checks against a substantially larger reader.
decisions.rejected: Implementing real anchors, aliases and merge keys — a hook config gains almost nothing from reuse syntax.

decisions.decision: Add a general check that the parser reached the last line, on top of the named-token checks
decisions.why: A cursor that stops short is the mechanism behind every silent truncation, so checking it converts the whole class — including shapes nobody has hit yet — into a loud failure.
decisions.rejected: Named-token detection alone, which only patches the four spellings we enumerated.

decisions.decision: Anchor the token checks to the first token of a key or an unquoted value
decisions.why: Keeps the change from narrowing: shell commands with && , quoted globs with * and redirects with > must keep parsing exactly as they do now.
decisions.rejected: Scanning the whole line for the marker characters, which would break the two things a hook config is most full of.

decisions.decision: Examine only the first token of a key or an unquoted value
decisions.why: A marker later in a value is ordinary text — shell commands with &&, redirects with >, quoted globs with * must all keep parsing exactly as before.
decisions.rejected: Scanning the whole line for the marker characters.

decisions.decision: Reject the whole file rather than apply the readable part
decisions.why: A partly applied config is the defect: the author reads their own file and believes all of it is live.
decisions.rejected: Applying what parsed and warning about the rest.

plan.summary: Plan to make an unreadable companion.yml raise so the existing malformed path reports it, with a completeness backstop covering the whole silent-truncation class.
plan.key_finding: The anchor is a symptom: the reader unwinds and returns whatever it collected whenever its cursor stops advancing, so the load-bearing fix is checking that the parser reached the last line.
